flights.title: Prometheus, Western Engineering, Spaceport America Cup 2022 (M1520)
flights.altimeter_evidence: an Altus Metrum TeleMetrum: its height column is the standard atmosphere's altitude of its pressure column less the first row's (the gap is below)
flights.example_drag_source: prometheus_2022_flight_sim.ipynb:224-261 (`prometheus_cd_at_ma` from Mach 0.15, where it starts to change, and power on 1.02 times it)
flights.note: flown in the weather of 24 June 2023, a year after the flight, as RocketPy's example flies it: RocketPy has no ERA5 file of the day. The log is read to 29.58 s: a pressure transient then drops the reading 600 m and returns it 8 m above the highest reading before
flights.explanation: consistent with hpr's drag. On the example's own drag, the team's table from Mach 0.15, the apogee is within the target. The reading is built on weather a year off the flight's day (the note). Against the satellite heights, hpr's conversion reads 1 to 2 points below the altimeter here and on Juno III, which flew in its own day's weather, so the wrong day's share of the miss can't be told apart.

flights.title: Juno III, Projeto Jupiter, Spaceport America Cup 2023 (the team's motor)
flights.altimeter_evidence: a Missile Works RRC3 (juno3/README.txt:21): its height column is the standard atmosphere's altitude of its pressure column less the first row's (the gap is below)
flights.example_drag_source: juno3_flight_sim.ipynb:244-251, :356-359 (`drag_curve.csv`, scaled to 0.38 at Mach 0.6 "from CFD analysis")
flights.note: the log is read to 24.60 s, as it levels off: a pressure transient there dips the reading by 94 m, then lifts it 62 m above the level within 0.3 s, to the 3213.4 m the team reports as its apogee, and the record's last two rows are corrupt. At the cut the log's own velocity column still reads 17.5 m/s up, so its apogee may be 10 m to 20 m low. The thrust file's last five points are negative (-6.8 to -47.3 N); hpr, which refuses a negative thrust, reads them as zero, and RocketPy's flight holds its thrust at zero too
flights.explanation: consistent with the motor's impulse. The notebook reshapes the team's own motor curve (`mandioca_thrust_curve.csv`) to 5.8 s and 8800 N s, 4.9% less than the file; on the file as recorded the apogee is within the target, and on the team's drag it is not.

flights.title: Cavour, Politecnico di Torino, EuRoC 2023 (L995)
flights.altimeter_evidence: the CATS Vega EuRoC 2023 required, its radio telemetry: the Kalman filter's height from a barometer and an accelerometer, sent in whole meters cut toward zero (as matched on its sister flights' logs), with no pressure; barometric assumed
flights.note: the log is read to 23.6 s, the first row the team's ground-station log tags Drogue: past it, the radio telemetry's filtered height rises 8 m in 0.2 s, to 2789 m, faster than the rocket can climb and about 2 s before the drogue channel's continuity is first lost (25.6 s); the coast's peak before it is 2785 m
flights.explanation: consistent with hpr's drag. On the example's own curves, labeled RASAero II, the apogee is within the target. hpr's drag is below them: at Mach 0.3, 8.3% below power off and 18.3% below power on (the aerodynamics page's comparison; the power-on gap's cause is open), and the design's fin edges are placeholders, since the example records none.

predicted_first.title: Astra, Faraday Rocketry UPV, EuRoC 2022 (L1350)
predicted_first.altimeter_evidence: the notebook calls it a COTS altimeter's flight (astra_flight_sim.ipynb:383-385), one row a second beside a latitude and a longitude, and records no more: barometric assumed, as hobby altimeters are
predicted_first.design: the design built from RocketPy's example, `rocketpy-astra`
predicted_first.reference_rule: the highest reading of the log's `alt` column, in meters, the log read whole
predicted_first.revised_because: M1.14b15 (ADR-363, decision 1) made the tip-off phase the default. Astra has two rail buttons, so between the forward button's leaving the rail and the aft one's it turns about the aft button, and it leaves the rail turning (ADR-357, ADR-358). Nothing in its design or inputs changed.

predicted_first.title: Andromeda, Aristotle Space and Aeronautics Team, EuRoC 2022 (the team's curve)
predicted_first.altimeter_evidence: the notebook calls it a COTS altimeter (andromeda_flight_sim.ipynb:459-461), logged in feet and in meters with a vertical speed, and records no more: barometric assumed, as hobby altimeters are
predicted_first.design: the design built from RocketPy's example, `rocketpy-andromeda`
predicted_first.reference_rule: the highest reading of the log's `alt(m)` column, the log read whole
predicted_first.revised_because: M1.14b15 (ADR-363, decision 1) made the tip-off phase the default. Andromeda has two rail buttons, so between the forward button's leaving the rail and the aft one's it turns about the aft button, and it leaves the rail turning (ADR-357, ADR-358). Nothing in its design or inputs changed.
untraced: the flight carried the team's air brakes, and no record says when or how far they opened: none is flown here, so any opening leaves this prediction high
the thrust file holds more impulse than the Cesaroni M2020 reload it is named for is certified at, so the notebook does not settle which motor the logged flight burned

predicted_first.title: Erebus 11, BME Suborbitals, EuRoC 2022 (a Cesaroni Pro54 K)
predicted_first.altimeter_evidence: the notebook calls it a COTS altimeter (erebus_flight_sim.ipynb:390-392), a file named filtered, and records no more: barometric assumed, as hobby altimeters are
predicted_first.design: the design built from RocketPy's example, `rocketpy-erebus-11`
predicted_first.reference_rule: the highest reading of the log's `alt` column, in meters, the log read whole
predicted_first.revised_because: Two changes to HPR Sim. M1.14i3 (ADR-362) changed its base drag below Mach 0.8: behind a boattail the base is d_B/d of a flat base's value (NASA TR R-100, 1961, p. 11), set on the Hermes A-3A's measured base drag (NACA RM SL55F15), where the old rule read 0.050 to 0.064 high on its largest cross-section and the new one 0.025 to 0.035. Erebus 11 has a boattail, and its apogee rose 46.0 m to 2760.1 m. Then M1.14b15 (ADR-363, decision 1) made the tip-off phase the default: Erebus 11 has two rail buttons and leaves the rail turning (ADR-357, ADR-358), which took 0.5 m off. Nothing in its design or inputs changed.

predicted_first.altimeter_evidence: the log's first line names a PerfectFlite altimeter, `PerfectFlite SLCF`, and a PerfectFlite has a barometer and no accelerometer (docs/format/pf2.md)
predicted_first.design: the design file `refs/public-flights/rocketry-files/macie/macie-xl.ork` as saved, as its stored simulation `maciexl-1-or` flies it
predicted_first.weather: the 1976 US Standard Atmosphere, for the stored simulation's `isa`
predicted_first.reference_rule: the apogee the altimeter worked out, in the log's header (its `Apogee:` line, in feet above the pad, 0.3048 m to the foot), which leaves out the ejection spike among the samples; never the highest sample
untraced: no record gives the day, its air and wind, or the rail, and of the site only each log's header gives the pad's height above sea level (12 ft for flight 1, 37 ft for flight 2): the stored simulation's are flown, its sea level among them, and all nine simulations in the file carry the same ones
no record says the rocket was weighed as flown: the file's parts and overrides are flown

the reader warns that the motor's curve file disagrees with ThrustCurve.org's record of the motor (the figures are in the flight's `reader_warnings` in the JSON); the file the design's digest names is flown

the motor flies the bundled catalog's masses for it, 313.6 g of propellant and 555.52 g loaded, as every catalog motor does, where the curve file the design's digest names, and OpenRocket's own record of that digest, give 310.016 g and 555.072 g (the table's `mass_difference`)
